title: Introduce dependency injection to remove hard-coded singletons
description: Several modules directly import and use a hard-coded singleton database client and a hard-coded singleton logger, making them impossible to unit test in isolation. Introduce constructor-based dependency injection for these dependencies while preserving a default-wiring path so existing top-level application startup code requires minimal changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Affected modules accept their database client and logger as constructor/factory parameters rather than importing singletons directly.
A default-wiring factory function preserves the previous singleton-based behavior for application startup.
Unit tests can now substitute a fake database client and logger without any module-level mocking of imports.
All existing integration tests pass using the default-wiring factory.
No remaining direct import of the singleton client or logger exists inside the affected modules' business logic.
verificationMethod: diff-analysis: confirm no remaining direct singleton imports in the affected modules, combined with a test-suite run of both new isolated unit tests and existing integration tests.
groundTruth: Affected modules are converted to accept dependencies via their constructor or a factory function; a createDefaultX() factory in the composition root wires the real singletons for production use, and tests use a separate factory call with fakes.
